changes.needle: Windows minidumps never contained the system profile.
changes.commitMessage:
Move SystemProfile minidump stream ownership to crash reporter client

The SystemProfile minidump user stream
(kSharedMemorySystemProfileMinidump) was owned by a process-wide
singleton in //components/metrics. On Windows, Crashpad is started by
chrome_elf.dll while metrics runs in chrome.dll, and each module ended
up with its own copy of the singleton: the Crashpad handler received
chrome_elf's region while metrics wrote into chrome.dll's. As a result,
Windows minidumps never contained the system profile.

Move ownership of the stream to Chrome's crash reporter client
(ChromeCrashReporterClient), which always lives in the module that
starts Crashpad, and let other modules write to it through
//components/crash:

- ChromeCrashUserStreams (//chrome/app), owned by
  ChromeCrashReporterClient, creates the shared memory and hands
  read-only handles to the handler via
  CrashReporterClient::GetUserStreamSharedMemoryRegions().
- Add CrashReporterClient::WriteUserStreamData() and
  crash_reporter::WriteUserStreamData() to update an embedder-owned
  stream by type. On Windows the call crosses into chrome_elf.dll
  through the new WriteUserStreamData_ExportThunk.
- //components/metrics no longer owns any shared memory.
  WriteSystemProfileUserStream() only pushes the serialized proto and
  records UMA.SystemProfile.UserStreamOverflow in the metrics module,
  since histograms recorded in chrome_elf.dll are not uploaded.

Tested: the write has two code paths, each checked by a manual test that
crashes the browser and the GPU process with the feature enabled and
inspects the minidumps:
- Cross-module path (Windows: chrome.dll -> export thunk ->
  chrome_elf.dll): ran it on a Windows 10 swarming bot. Both minidumps
  contain user stream 0x4B6B0003, which decodes to a valid
  SystemProfileProto.
- Same-module path (Linux, ChromeOS, Mac, Android, which share the posix
  ChromeCrashReporterClient) checked on Linux. The stream is present in
  both minidumps. The per-platform transport of the regions to the
  handler is not changed by this CL.

changes.needle: Share the feature list startup between Chrome and iOS
changes.commitMessage:
[variations] Share the feature list startup between Chrome and iOS

Chrome and iOS run the same startup sequence up to
base::FeatureList::SetInstance(). Previously, ChromeFeatureListCreator
and IOSChromeMainParts maintained separate copies of those startup
steps.

Add variations::CreateFeatureList(FeatureListCreatorClient&) in
components/variations/feature_list_creator to run the shared sequence.
When --no-experiments is absent, CreateFeatureList() converts
about:flags entries to switches and registers flag variation parameters.
CreateFeatureList() also refreshes command-line crash keys, creates
MetricsServicesManager, and calls VariationsService::SetUpFieldTrials().

Consolidate adjacent startup helpers across components, Chrome, and iOS.
Move kNoExperiments to components/webui/flags, add
NetworkTimeTracker::CreateUninitialized(), and add
variations::CreateVariationsIdsProvider() for Chrome, Android, and iOS.
Move Local State store setup into chrome_prefs::CreateLocalState() and
move Windows locale and Desktop seed helpers into first_run. Move
Android first-run seed retrieval into ChromeVariationsServiceClient and
clear ChromeFeatureListCreator client pointers on handoff.

Each embedder creates Local State and the policy connector before
CreateFeatureList() and retains MetricsServicesManager ownership.

changes.needle: proof of concept for capturing early exit metrics
changes.commitMessage:
[DO NOT SUBMIT] proof of concept for capturing early exit metrics

This CL:

1. Moves the Persistent Histogram System initialization earlier (as is
   done in crrev.com/c/3950551)
2. Immediately writes a "bare" system_profile to the PMA file after
   initialization

step 2 is done very hackily, just to show that the system profile
fields of interest are accessible at that stage in Chrome

-----
To test this CL:

(Assumes you have metrics reporting enabled. You can run Chrome with
--force-enable-metrics-reporting flag otherwise.)

1. uncomment lines 1610-1611 in chrome/app/chrome_main_delegate.cc to
   simulate an early exit (also emits a histogram right before)
2. build and run Chrome, which should close as soon as it runs
3. comment lines 1610-1611 in chrome/app/chrome_main_delegate.cc
4. go to chrome://metrics-internals
5. after ~1minute, an independent log should be produced (maybe more
   depending on the amount of PMA files you have on disk; if that's
   the case, wait until no more independent logs are being created)
6. export the logs
7. inspect the independent log in http://shortn/_4KyQkdYE5L (Google
   internal)
8. confirm that the "Test.Test" histogram has been emitted (its hash
   is 8403475912766526277)

Change-Id: Ie6dce09ce6bb6eb657d3a2c4521b359b91f932bd
